summary: Radar for 2026-10-25, GLP-1 focus only. The best opening is efpeglenatide, sold as Eppe. South Korea's MFDS approved it on Oct 8 for adults with obesity who don't have diabetes, and Hanmi has said it will launch around Oct 29. It's a new drug name with published Phase 3 numbers: 448 Korean adults, 9.02% average weight loss versus 0.89% on placebo at 40 weeks. I found almost no English explainers, so it matches the EloraTZP pattern. Make it a 'What Is Efpeglenatide?' long-form timed to the launch (Lane C if the launch news is under 48 hours old). Second is elecoglipron, AstraZeneca's once-daily pill. Note: it is not a Lilly drug. A new Phase 1 food-effect paper came out Oct 19, and the Phase 2 results are public, so it can be the weekly 'What Is [new drug]?' test. Retatrutide still has the highest Short peaks. Sleep apnea (TRIUMPH-OSA, NEJM Oct 20) is still being picked up (Medical Xpress Oct 24). It is now about 5 days old, so it's past Lane C; make it a Short only if we haven't already. The gray-market angle got new pickup (Futurism lab analysis Oct 24, News24 South Africa Oct 25), but we have to decide which single dated fact goes in this week's one recall/gray-market Short. Evergreen Lane A topics are still steady: tirzepatide side effects, refreshed by an Oct 22 review of how trials measure nausea and an Oct GI-motility paper; muscle and protein; stopping. Halloween (Oct 31) and Thanksgiving are close, so seasonal Shorts should go out now. Three things I checked and dropped: the 'FDA approves Lilly pill' headline is the April 1 Foundayo approval, not new; the Novo v. Lilly ads lawsuit dates from July; and I couldn't confirm Lilly's Q3 date. Rejected: microdosing and 'research-grade retatrutide sourcing' pieces.

candidates.topic: What is efpeglenatide (Eppe)? Hanmi's weekly GLP-1 approved in South Korea for adults with obesity without diabetes (MFDS, Oct 8, 2026), with launch expected around Oct 29
candidates.angle: 'What Is Efpeglenatide? The New Weekly GLP-1 Explained' (generic name first). The Phase 3 trial: 448 Korean adults without diabetes, 9.02% average weight loss versus 0.89% on placebo at week 40, and 75.1% losing at least 5% versus 13.5%. Common side effects with trial rates: diarrhoea 17.6%, nausea 16.6%, indigestion 15.6%, constipation 14.6%, vomiting 11.6%. Dated status: approved in South Korea only; no FDA, MHRA, TGA or Health Canada filing announced. Frame it as 'smaller weight loss than tirzepatide in separate trials, not head-to-head'. Funnel Short at 20:00 the day the long-form goes live.
candidates.predicted_peak: 3–10 days (launch news around Oct 29, then Korean price coverage)
candidates.why_now: It's a brand-new drug name with approval plus a launch date, Hanmi plans to launch at the end of October, and I found almost no English-language video explainers. That's the same setup as EloraTZP (523 views, 61% of our GLP-1 long-form views).

candidates.topic: What is elecoglipron? AstraZeneca's once-daily oral GLP-1 pill: Phase 2 VISTA weight results plus a new Phase 1 fed-versus-fasted study (Br J Clin Pharmacol, Oct 19, 2026)
candidates.angle: 'What Is Elecoglipron? The Next GLP-1 Pill, Explained': how it differs from the semaglutide pill (no food or water restriction reported), Phase 2 weight loss of 2.6% to 10.5% across doses at 26 weeks (VISTA, adults with obesity), and the SOLSTICE type 2 diabetes trial (404 adults). The new Phase 1 food-effect study in healthy volunteers covers pharmacokinetics only. Status: investigational, not approved anywhere. Credit it to AstraZeneca, not Lilly.
